To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

customer satisfaction is a function of expectations, quality, price, and market share; that customer satisfaction is positively related to profitability; and that market share is negatively related to customer satisfaction.
customer satisfaction is an important determinant of economic returns.

(a) customer satisfaction is a function of the gap between the customer's expectations and the actual quality of the firm's products, (b) this relationship is stronger when the firm's products are of high quality, (c) customer satisfaction has a significant impact on profitability, (d) the market's expectations about the quality of the firm have a significant effect on customer satisfaction, (e) market share has a negative effect on customer satisfaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the economic consequences of improving quality and customer satisfaction.
the link between customer expectations of a firm's quality, the actual quality of a firm, customer satisfaction with the firm, market share, and profitability.
the relationship between customer satisfaction and profitability, and it provides evidence that customer satisfaction does affect profitability.

customer satisfaction is an important driver of profitability, but that it is not the only one.
the economic benefits of increased customer satisfaction are significant and that firms should focus their attention on improving customer satisfaction.
the link between customer and shareholder satisfaction is strong and positive.

the economic benefits of quality and customer satisfaction can be substantial.
customer satisfaction is a key determinant of profitability.
there are economic benefits of improving customer satisfaction.
